questions.q: In which year was Hagia Sophia in Constantinople completed?
questions.note: Finished in 537 after less than six years of building, its soaring dome went unmatched anywhere for almost a thousand years.

questions.q: In which year was the Diamond Sutra, the world's oldest dated printed book, produced in China?
questions.note: The scroll carries a date equivalent to 11 May 868, nearly six centuries before Gutenberg's press.

questions.q: In which year was the Domesday Book, William the Conqueror's great survey of England, completed?
questions.note: Compiled in 1086, it recorded over 13,000 English places in such detail that it was still cited in courts centuries later.

questions.q: In which year was Magna Carta sealed by King John at Runnymede?
questions.note: King John sealed Magna Carta in 1215, and four original copies of that first issue still survive today.

questions.q: In which year was Beijing's Forbidden City completed?
questions.note: Completed in 1420 after 14 years of work, it served as home to 24 emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties.

questions.q: In which year did Johannes Gutenberg complete his famous printed Bible in Mainz?
questions.note: Gutenberg's Bible was completed around 1455, and a single page could now be printed faster than a scribe wrote a line.

questions.q: In which year did Vasco da Gama reach India, opening the first sea route there from Europe?
questions.note: Da Gama anchored near Calicut in May 1498 after ten months at sea, linking Europe and Asia by ocean for the first time.

questions.q: In which year did the Great Fire of London break out in a bakery on Pudding Lane?
questions.note: The fire of 1666 destroyed more than 13,000 houses yet, remarkably, only a handful of deaths were ever recorded.

questions.q: In which year did the Montgolfier brothers' hot-air balloon carry the first humans into the sky?
questions.note: In November 1783 two Frenchmen drifted over Paris for 25 minutes, and human flight began with a paper-lined balloon.

questions.q: In which year did Britain issue the Penny Black, the world's first adhesive postage stamp?
questions.note: The Penny Black went on sale in 1840, and about 68 million were printed in its single year of use.

questions.q: In which year did the world's first underground railway open in London?
questions.note: The Metropolitan Railway opened in 1863, carrying 38,000 passengers behind steam locomotives on its first day.

questions.q: In which year did construction begin on King Ludwig II's Neuschwanstein Castle in Bavaria?
questions.note: Work began in 1869 on the fairy-tale castle that later inspired Disneyland's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

questions.q: In which year did the Orient Express make its first journey from Paris?
questions.note: The famous train first steamed out of Paris in 1883, bound for Constantinople with velvet seats and five-course dinners.

questions.q: In which year did the Eiffel Tower open as the gateway to a Paris world's fair?
questions.note: Opened for the 1889 Exposition Universelle, the tower was meant to stand for just 20 years but proved too useful to demolish.

questions.q: In which year did the Lumière brothers hold the first public film screening in Paris?
questions.note: In December 1895 the brothers charged one franc to watch ten short films, and cinema was born in a Paris basement.

questions.q: In which year did Roald Amundsen's expedition become the first to reach the South Pole?
questions.note: Amundsen planted the Norwegian flag at the pole on 14 December 1911, with all his men and dogs skiing home safely.

questions.q: In which year did Howard Carter discover the tomb of Tutankhamun?
questions.note: Peering into the tomb by candlelight in 1922, Carter famously reported seeing 'wonderful things'.

questions.q: In which year did Amelia Earhart become the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic?
questions.source: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
questions.note: Earhart crossed alone in 1932, landing in a field in Northern Ireland where a farmhand asked if she had flown far.

questions.q: In which year was the 17th-century Swedish ship Vasa raised from Stockholm harbour?
questions.note: Vasa was lifted in 1961 after 333 years underwater, so well preserved that 98 per cent of the ship is original.

questions.q: In which year did farmers digging a well discover China's Terracotta Army?
questions.note: Farmers struck pottery fragments in 1974 and uncovered one of the greatest archaeological finds of the 20th century.

questions.q: In which year was the wreck of the Titanic finally located on the Atlantic seabed?
questions.note: A team led by Robert Ballard found the wreck in 1985, 73 years after the ship went down.

questions.q: How tall was the Great Pyramid of Giza when it was completed?
questions.note: It originally rose about 147 metres, though losing its casing stones has trimmed it to roughly 138 today.

questions.q: For about how many years did the Great Pyramid remain the tallest man-made structure on Earth?
questions.note: It held the record for some 3,800 years, until England's Lincoln Cathedral finally overtook it around 1311.

questions.q: How long is the Great Sphinx of Giza?
questions.note: The Sphinx stretches about 73 metres from paw to tail, carved from a single ridge of limestone.

questions.q: How much does Tutankhamun's gold funerary mask weigh?
questions.note: The mask weighs 10.23 kilograms of solid gold, inlaid with lapis lazuli and coloured glass.

questions.q: How much does the Rosetta Stone weigh?
questions.note: The granodiorite slab weighs about 760 kilograms and carries the same decree in three scripts.

questions.q: About how many spectators could Rome's Colosseum hold?
questions.note: Around 50,000 Romans could pack in, filing through 80 numbered entrances in a matter of minutes.

questions.q: How wide is the concrete dome of the Pantheon in Rome?
questions.note: At 43.3 metres across, it is still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome, nearly 1,900 years on.

questions.q: How long is Hadrian's Wall, built by the Romans across northern England?
questions.note: The wall ran about 117 kilometres from coast to coast, with a small fort at every Roman mile.

questions.q: How many columns surround the outer colonnade of the Parthenon in Athens?
questions.note: There are 46 outer columns, each subtly curved because the architects knew perfectly straight lines look bent.

questions.q: About how many spectators could the ancient Greek theatre of Epidaurus seat?
questions.note: Its 55 rows held some 14,000 people, and the acoustics still let the back row hear a match struck on stage.

questions.q: In which year BC were the first recorded ancient Olympic Games held at Olympia?
questions.note: The first recorded Games of 776 BC had a single event, a sprint of about 192 metres won by a cook named Coroebus.

questions.q: How many bronze gears survive in the ancient Greek Antikythera mechanism?
questions.note: At least 30 interlocking gears survive in the 2,000-year-old device, which predicted eclipses like a clockwork computer.

questions.q: How tall is the Pyramid of the Sun at Teotihuacan in Mexico?
questions.note: The Pyramid of the Sun rises about 65 metres, built by a city whose original name is still unknown.

questions.q: About how many years old is Ötzi the Iceman, discovered in the Alps in 1991?
questions.note: Ötzi died about 5,300 years ago, and the ice preserved everything down to his 61 tattoos and his last meal.

questions.q: How much does an average sarsen stone at Stonehenge weigh?
questions.note: The sarsens average about 25 tonnes each and were hauled some 25 kilometres to the site around 4,500 years ago.

questions.q: How many kilometres of the Great Wall of China were mapped by the official 2012 survey?
questions.source: China State Administration of Cultural Heritage
questions.note: The 2012 survey measured 21,196 kilometres of walls and trenches, roughly half the circumference of the Earth.

questions.q: About how many life-size warriors are estimated to stand in the Terracotta Army?
questions.note: An estimated 8,000 clay soldiers guard the First Emperor's tomb, and no two faces are alike.

questions.q: How long is China's Grand Canal, the longest artificial waterway on Earth?
questions.note: The canal runs about 1,794 kilometres from Beijing to Hangzhou, with sections dug 2,500 years ago.

questions.q: How many buildings stand within Beijing's Forbidden City?
questions.note: The complex contains 980 buildings, and tradition claims 9,999 and a half rooms so as not to rival heaven's 10,000.

questions.q: How large is the Angkor Wat temple complex in Cambodia?
questions.note: At about 162 hectares, Angkor Wat is the largest temple complex on Earth, moat and all.

questions.q: About how many workers built the Taj Mahal?
questions.note: Some 20,000 workers laboured for over two decades, helped by a reported 1,000 elephants hauling marble.

questions.q: How many days after leaving Spain in August 1492 did Columbus first sight land in the Americas?
questions.note: Land was sighted on 12 October 1492, 70 days after the three ships left Palos, including a stop in the Canaries.

questions.q: How many crewmen completed the first circumnavigation of the globe aboard the ship Victoria in 1522?
questions.note: Just 18 weather-beaten sailors brought Victoria home in 1522, three years after five ships had set out.

questions.q: How many years did Marco Polo spend away from Venice on his journey through Asia?
questions.note: Polo was away 24 years, and Venetians nicknamed him 'Il Milione' for his tales of a million marvels.

questions.q: About how many kilometres did the 14th-century Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta cover on his journeys?
questions.note: Ibn Battuta logged an estimated 120,000 kilometres over 29 years, more than any traveller before the steam age.

questions.q: By how many days did Amundsen's team beat Scott's to the South Pole?
questions.note: Amundsen arrived on 14 December 1911, a full 34 days before Scott's party reached the pole.

questions.q: How many kilometres did Shackleton's open-boat voyage from Elephant Island to South Georgia cover in 1916?
questions.note: The 6-man crew of the James Caird sailed about 1,300 kilometres through the Southern Ocean, and every one of Shackleton's men came home.

questions.q: How many days did Thor Heyerdahl's Kon-Tiki raft take to cross from Peru to Polynesia in 1947?
questions.note: The balsa raft drifted for 101 days and nearly 7,000 kilometres before running onto a Polynesian reef.

questions.q: How long was the RMS Titanic?
questions.note: At 269 metres, Titanic was the largest ship afloat in 1912, longer than three football pitches.

questions.q: How many lifeboats did the Titanic carry on her maiden voyage?
questions.note: She carried 20 lifeboats, which was actually four more than the outdated regulations of the day required.

questions.q: At what depth does the wreck of the Titanic lie in the Atlantic?
questions.note: The wreck rests about 3,800 metres down, so deep that sunlight has never reached it.

questions.q: How many years did Queen Victoria reign?
questions.note: Victoria reigned 63 years, a record for a British monarch that stood until Elizabeth II passed it in 2015.

questions.q: How many years did Louis XIV, the Sun King, reign over France?
questions.note: Crowned at age four, Louis XIV reigned 72 years, the longest of any major European monarch.

questions.q: How many years did Queen Elizabeth II reign?
questions.note: Elizabeth II reigned 70 years, celebrating a Platinum Jubilee no British monarch had ever reached.

questions.q: How many years did King Sobhuza II of Swaziland reign, the longest verified reign in history?
questions.note: Sobhuza II reigned 82 years from 1899 to 1982, having come to the throne at four months old.

questions.q: How many years passed between the start and the completion of Cologne Cathedral?
questions.note: Begun in 1248 and finished in 1880, the cathedral took 632 years, with work paused for over three centuries.

questions.q: How many years did it take to build St Peter's Basilica in Rome?
questions.note: Construction ran 120 years from 1506 to 1626, outlasting twenty popes and employing Michelangelo along the way.

questions.q: How many years elapsed between the start and the completion of the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
questions.note: Wars and pauses stretched the build to 199 years, and the long breaks let the soil settle enough to save the tilting tower.

questions.q: How tall is the steeple of Ulm Minster in Germany, the world's tallest church tower?
questions.note: Completed in 1890, the steeple reaches 161.5 metres, and 768 steps lead up to its viewing gallery.

questions.q: About how many rooms does Windsor Castle contain?
questions.note: Windsor has about 1,000 rooms and is the oldest and largest occupied castle in the world.

questions.q: How many rooms does the Palace of Versailles contain?
questions.note: The palace counts 2,300 rooms, having grown from what began as Louis XIII's modest hunting lodge.

questions.q: How many mirrors line the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles?
questions.note: Its 17 arches hold 357 mirrors, a dazzling extravagance when mirrors cost more than paintings.

questions.q: How many people visited the Great Exhibition of 1851 in London's Crystal Palace?
questions.source: Royal Commission for the Exhibition of 1851
questions.note: Six million visitors came in five months, equal to about a third of Britain's population at the time.

questions.q: How tall was the original Ferris Wheel, built for the 1893 Chicago World's Fair?
questions.note: George Ferris's wheel stood about 80 metres tall, and each of its 36 cars could carry 60 people.

questions.q: How many steps lead from the ground to the very top of the Eiffel Tower?
questions.note: There are 1,665 steps to the summit, though visitors have only ever been allowed to climb partway.

questions.q: How tall is the Atomium, built in Brussels for the 1958 World's Fair?
questions.note: The Atomium stands 102 metres tall and depicts an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.

questions.q: How many people visited Expo 2010 in Shanghai, the best-attended world's fair in history?
questions.note: Expo 2010 drew 73 million visitors in six months, with over a million passing the gates on its busiest day.

questions.q: How tall is the Arc de Triomphe in Paris, completed in 1836?
questions.note: The arch rises 50 metres, and in 1919 a daring aviator flew a biplane clean through it.

questions.q: How many seconds did the Wright brothers' first powered flight last in 1903?
questions.source: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
questions.note: The first flight lasted just 12 seconds and covered 37 metres, shorter than the wingspan of a modern jumbo jet.

questions.q: How many minutes did Louis Blériot take to fly across the English Channel in 1909?
questions.note: Blériot crossed from Calais to Dover in about 37 minutes, winning a £1,000 newspaper prize and lasting fame.

questions.q: About how many hours did Alcock and Brown's first non-stop transatlantic flight take in 1919?
questions.note: The pair flew from Newfoundland to Ireland in about 16 hours, landing nose-first in a soft Irish bog.

questions.q: How many hours did Charles Lindbergh's solo flight from New York to Paris take in 1927?
questions.source: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
questions.note: Lindbergh flew alone for 33.5 hours, fighting sleep by flying low enough to feel the sea spray.

questions.q: At what speed did Concorde cruise on its supersonic passenger flights?
questions.note: Concorde cruised at about 2,180 km/h, twice the speed of sound, crossing the Atlantic in under three and a half hours.

questions.q: About how many days did the airship Graf Zeppelin take to fly around the world in 1929?
questions.note: The round-the-world flight took about 21 days, including a single non-stop leg from Germany to Japan.

questions.q: What was the top speed of Carl Benz's 1886 Patent-Motorwagen, the first true automobile?
questions.note: The three-wheeled Motorwagen managed 16 km/h, and Bertha Benz drove it 100 km to prove the invention worked.

questions.q: What top speed did Stephenson's Rocket reach at the 1829 Rainhill Trials?
questions.note: Rocket hit about 48 km/h, an astonishing speed to onlookers who had never moved faster than a galloping horse.

questions.q: How long was the Suez Canal when it opened in 1869?
questions.note: The canal opened at 164 kilometres long, cutting the London-to-Bombay voyage by around 7,000 kilometres.

questions.q: How many lines of text appear on most pages of the Gutenberg Bible?

questions.q: How many copies of the Gutenberg Bible are known to survive?

questions.q: How tall is the Mona Lisa painting in the Louvre?

questions.q: How many years did Michelangelo spend painting the Sistine Chapel ceiling?

questions.q: How long is the Bayeux Tapestry, which tells the story of the Norman Conquest?
questions.note: The embroidered cloth runs 68.38 metres, stitched with 58 scenes, 623 people and over 700 animals.

questions.q: How much does Big Ben, the great bell of Westminster, weigh?

questions.q: How many islands is the historic city of Venice built on?

questions.q: How many nations competed at the first modern Olympic Games in Athens in 1896?

questions.q: How many moai statues have been documented on Easter Island?

questions.q: How many steps do the staircases and top platform of El Castillo at Chichén Itzá add up to?

questions.q: How tall is the rock-cut facade of the Treasury at Petra in Jordan?

questions.q: How many years did the Hundred Years' War between England and France actually last?

questions.q: How many prisoners were inside the Bastille when it was stormed in 1789?
questions.note: Just 7 — four forgers, two men held as insane, and one aristocrat.

questions.q: In which year did Henry VIII's flagship Mary Rose sink in the Solent?

questions.q: How many prints make up Hokusai's celebrated series 'Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji'?

questions.q: In which year was the Battle of Hastings?
questions.note: 1066 — the Norman Conquest, later stitched into the Bayeux Tapestry.

questions.q: In which year did Shakespeare's original Globe Theatre open in London?

questions.q: In which year did euro banknotes and coins enter circulation?
questions.note: 1 January 2002, across twelve countries at once — the biggest cash changeover in history.

questions.q: Around which year did Vikings settle at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland?
questions.note: Around AD 1000 — the sagas' Vinland, confirmed by archaeologists in 1960.

questions.q: In which year did Hiram Bingham bring Machu Picchu to the world's attention?
questions.note: 1911 — his 'lost city of the Incas' had never been lost to local farmers.

questions.q: In which year was The Wizard of Oz first released in cinemas?
questions.note: The Wizard of Oz arrived in 1939, whisking audiences from sepia Kansas into glorious Technicolor Oz.

questions.q: In which year did Walt Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the first full-length cel-animated feature, premiere?

questions.q: In which year was Toy Story, the first entirely computer-animated feature film, released?
questions.note: Toy Story opened in 1995, taking animation to infinity and beyond without a single hand-drawn frame.

questions.q: In which year was the original Star Wars film released?
questions.note: Star Wars landed in 1977, and queues around the block turned a space fantasy into a cultural phenomenon.

questions.q: In which year did Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park stomp into cinemas?
questions.note: Jurassic Park opened in 1993, its computer-generated dinosaurs convincing audiences that life had found a way.

questions.q: In which year did Casablanca premiere?

questions.q: In which year was the film The Sound of Music released?

questions.q: In which year was E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial released?

questions.q: In which year was the musical Singin' in the Rain released?

questions.q: In which year was the first Academy Awards ceremony held?

questions.q: In which year did Mickey Mouse make his sound-cartoon debut in Steamboat Willie?

questions.q: In which year did the sitcom I Love Lucy first air on American television?

questions.q: In which year did the science-fiction series Doctor Who first air on the BBC?
questions.note: Doctor Who first materialised in 1963, the day after President Kennedy's assassination dominated the news.

questions.q: In which year did Sesame Street first air on television?
questions.note: Sesame Street opened its doors in 1969, teaching letters and numbers with a little help from some Muppets.

questions.q: In which year did The Simpsons premiere as a half-hour television series?

questions.q: In which year was the original King Kong film released?
questions.note: King Kong climbed the newly built Empire State Building on screen in 1933, thanks to pioneering stop-motion animation.

questions.q: In which year was Disney's Frozen released?

questions.q: In which year was Studio Ghibli's Spirited Away first released in Japan?

questions.q: In which year was The Matrix released?
questions.note: The Matrix bent time in 1999, and its bullet-dodging 'bullet time' effect was imitated for years afterwards.

questions.q: In which year was Superman: The Movie, starring Christopher Reeve, released?

questions.q: In which year did The Muppet Show first air?

questions.q: How many Academy Awards did the 1959 epic Ben-Hur win?

questions.q: How many Academy Award nominations did the 1997 film Titanic receive?

questions.q: How many Academy Awards did Walt Disney win during his career, the most of any individual?

questions.q: How many Best Actress Oscars did Katharine Hepburn win, the record for any performer?

questions.q: As of 2024, how many Oscar nominations had composer John Williams received?

questions.q: Roughly how many minutes did the very first Academy Awards ceremony in 1929 last?

questions.q: How much does an Oscar statuette weigh in kilograms?

questions.q: How many Academy Awards did Slumdog Millionaire win in 2009?

questions.q: Roughly how many minutes did the standing ovation last when Charlie Chaplin received his honorary Oscar in 1972?
